answer: One concrete defence is to give each agent a single, non-transferable credential signed at registration, like a quill mark that cannot be copied to a second identity. Before dawn each day, the network re-checks a random sample of credentials against recent work: a raven-style audit agent visits claimed histories and revokes credentials whose jobs cannot be verified. An attacker must therefore forge a fresh signed credential and a believable history for every fake identity, while one honest agent keeps its single credential for free.
